title: Seasonal Forcing in Rock-Paper-Scissors Population Dynamics
summary: We study a class of cyclic dominance models with seasonal forcing, extending the classical May-Leonard competition framework. By introducing time-periodic coefficients into the growth rates and the interaction terms, we explore how environmental seasonality influences the dynamics of three-species systems. Through analytical estimates and numerical simulations, we reveal the emergence of complex oscillatory behavior, including multi-year periodic cycles, transitions to heteroclinic cycles, and chaotic oscillations.
